note: Schnabel et al. (2023) specifically report 5/5 affected individuals with homozygous truncating variants presenting with generalized congenital contractures involving upper and lower limb joints (shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee, foot).

evidence.text: Schnabel et al. report five affected individuals from three independent families with homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 who all shared congenital contractures involving shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee, and foot.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism. Using exome sequencing, we identified homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 in all patients.

numbers.metric: affected individuals with generalized joint contractures

evidence.text: Roos et al. describe homozygous FILIP1 variants causing congenital myopathy and contractures affecting both upper and lower limbs (elbow, fingers, knee, foot).

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: kyphoscoliosis, elbow and knee flexion contractures and bilateral foot pronation as well as flexion contractures of the fingers (i–iv).
